t.1.150.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Bhīma had promised, "I will do it," O Bhārata, then all the Pāṇḍavas came back, bringing the alms they had gathered.
t.1.150.2: Understanding him from his demeanor alone, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Pāṇḍu, then sat down alone in private and questioned his mother.
t.1.150.3: What deed does this Bhīma of terrible prowess intend to do? Is it with your consent that he wishes to do something here?
t.1.150.4: At my word alone this scorcher of foes will perform a great deed for the sake of the brāhmaṇa and for the deliverance of the city.
t.1.150.5: What is this rash and harsh misdeed that you have committed, lady? For the virtuous do not praise the abandonment of a son.
t.1.150.6: How can you wish to give up your own son for the sake of another's son? By abandoning your son, you would indeed be doing what is contrary to the ways of the world.
t.1.150.7: He on whose arms we all rely as we sleep in comfort, and through whom we seek to take back once more the kingdom that was seized by base men.
t.1.150.8: He of boundless might, brooding on whose valor Duryodhana, together with Śakuni, does not sleep any night for grief.
t.1.150.9: By whose heroic might, that of this hero, we were freed from the house of lac and from other evils as well, and by whom Purocana was slain.
t.1.150.10: Relying on whose valor we consider this earth, full of wealth, as already won, once we have slain the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
t.1.150.12: Yudhiṣṭhira, you should not grieve on account of Vṛkodara. This resolve was not made by me out of weakness of understanding.
t.1.150.11: Relying on what reasoning have you resolved upon giving him up? Surely your mind has not been thrown into confusion by sorrows, so that your wits have left you?
t.1.150.13: Here in the brahmin's house we have lived happily, my son; this, dear child, is the requital for it that I have considered. A man is only worth as much as this: that a kindness done to him does not perish.
t.1.150.14: Having seen the great prowess of that fearsome one back then at the house of lac, and from the slaying of Hiḍimba as well, I have full confidence in Vṛkodara.
t.1.150.15: For the strength of Bhīma's arms is great, equal to that of ten thousand elephants, the strength by which you, mighty as elephants, were carried out of Vāraṇāvata.
t.1.150.17: Long ago, when he was just born, he fell from my lap onto a mountain, and because of the heaviness of his body the rock was crushed to powder by his limbs.
t.1.150.16: There is no other with the strength of Vṛkodara; none such has been, nor will there be, one who could rise up in battle even against the foremost, the wielder of the thunderbolt himself.
t.1.150.19: This has not been decided out of greed, nor out of ignorance, nor out of delusion; rather, I have made this resolve for the sake of dharma deliberately, with full understanding.
t.1.150.18: Having considered that with wisdom, O Pāṇḍava, the strength of Bhīma and the repayment owed to the brahmin, I then made up my mind.
t.1.150.20: Both aims will be accomplished, Yudhiṣṭhira: the repayment for our lodging, and a great act of dharma performed.
t.1.150.21: I have heard that a kṣatriya who at any time renders aid to a brāhmaṇa in his affairs would attain auspicious worlds.
t.1.150.22: A kṣatriya who rescues a kṣatriya from death attains great fame in this world and in the next.
t.1.150.23: But a kṣatriya who renders aid in battle even to a vaiśya surely gladdens the people in all the worlds.
t.1.150.24: A king who rescues a śūdra who has come to him seeking refuge obtains, here in this world, birth in a family that is wealthy and honoured by kings.
t.1.150.26: Mother, what you have done after careful deliberation is fitting; you have done this out of compassion for the distressed brāhmaṇa. Surely this Bhīma will return after slaying the man-eater.
t.1.150.25: Thus did the blessed Vyāsa, exceedingly wise, speak long ago, O delight of the Kauravas; therefore this has been resolved upon.
t.1.150.27: But so that the men who dwell in the city may not come to know of this, this brahmin must be spoken to and carefully won over.
